exposure: number of previous pregnancies of mothers
cohort: The study included 4658 consecutive neonates born at the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology at the University of Szeged between June 2013 and July 2015, who underwent a whole-body skin examination within the first 72 hours of extrauterine life.
finding: The study found several significant correlations between the examined maternal and neonatal factors and the occurrence of birthmarks and neonatal skin disorders.
cross-section timing: within the first 72 hours of extrauterine life
birth_weight: Birth weight of neonates was measured as an exposure variable for all participants.
gest_age: Gestational age of neonates was measured as an exposure variable for all participants.
